_note: Column divider positions for Repertoire tables, as fractions of the CROPPED table width (apply docs/repertoire_crop_bounds.json first). Derived 2026-09-08 by taking the median of pipeline/row_detect._detect_vertical_dividers across every page of a group -- steadier than one visual reading, and within a group the positions vary by only 1-2% of width against columns 17-25% wide. Spread seasons (1890-91..1897-98) are keyed by season, put the DATE column at the table's RIGHT edge, and have 5 theaters. Single-page seasons (1898-99 onward) are keyed 'season:parity' because the recto/verso gutter offset shifts the table within a season crop (splitting by parity drops sigma from 0.056 to ~0.020); they put the DATE column at the LEFT and have 3 theaters. Groups are gated on even spacing, since theaters are equal-width -- check 'evenly_spaced' and 'source' before trusting one. NOTE on the final divider of spread seasons: it bounds the DATE column, which is NARROWER than a theater, so extrapolating it by one theater width overshoots. 1890-91 (0.966) and 1891-92 (0.982) overshot into the date column itself and were corrected against the page to 0.900 and 0.945; the rest landed in a consistent 0.918-0.943 band. Spread seasons therefore fail the even-spacing check by design. IMPORTANT: these fractions are relative to the CROPPED width, so any change to docs/repertoire_crop_bounds.json invalidates them and they must be rescaled or re-derived. 1891-92, 1898-99 and 1902-03 were rescaled on 2026-09-08 for exactly this reason. ADDENDUM 2026-09-09 (docs/eval/known_issues.md #69/#70): these values are no longer applied as a blind absolute template. The first position in each group's `dividers` list is now an ANCHOR/PRIOR, not a trusted final position: pipeline/row_detect.detect_columns refines it per page via `_refine_divider0`, which detects the real divider fresh and picks the candidate closest to this anchor within a small tolerance -- this is what the Gate 3 defect (kopecks truncated on 23-82% of even pages in several seasons, because the table's true position wanders by up to 0.11 of crop width within one group) needed, and a blind template alone could not give it. The remaining `dividers` entries are NOT used directly at all anymore -- only the GAPS between them are (season-level column widths, confirmed stable to 1-2% of table width, including on the two groups -- 1902-03:1 and 1907-08 -- that an earlier pass could not get automatic per-page detection to agree on for every divider). Per-page detection alone is not the fix either: a fully unconstrained search on repertoire_1907-08_p011 locked onto five evenly-spaced, 100%-confidence false candidates from faint paper staining in an oversized margin, ahead of the real divider -- the anchor is what lets the search reject that. Every value below therefore still matters (as the anchor + the gap template), and none needed re-measuring for this change; only the CODE that consumes them changed. Validated 2026-09-09 against 1902-03:1, 1907-08:0, 1907-08:1 (the two previously-stuck groups), 1898-99 and 1906-07 (both parities, as a regression check), and 1893-94 (spread format) -- 26 pages, every group producing the correct theater count with consistent widths, including repertoire_1907-08_p011 itself. ADDENDUM 2026-09-11 (fold-split extraction plan, Phase 4): 16 new "<season>:<parity>" entries added, format "spread_split", for the 8 spread seasons two-page-spread pages once physically split at the binding fold (pipeline/split_spread_pages.py). These are NOT the same geometry as the plain "<season>" spread entries above (those are fit to the whole unsplit two-leaf image) -- measured fresh against actual split half-images via _refine_dividers, seeded from the whole-spread dividers as an anchor/gap prior only. Keyed by parity exactly like the single-page seasons, and it works out cleanly: every split halfs own real printed page number is even for the top half and odd for the bottom half, confirmed with zero exceptions across all 182 halves checked, so parity_of() already resolves top vs bottom correctly with no code changes. Two seasons (1891-92, 1893-94) showed a real, non-noise divergence between top and bottom geometry and get genuinely different :0/:1 values; the other 6 seasons converge to the same value for both parities (kept as two identical entries only for lookup-key consistency). 1890-91 could not be verified this way at all -- _refine_dividers found zero gap-consistent candidates on every single sampled half (100% fallback) -- so its two entries just carry the old whole-spread numbers forward as an unverified prior; see _needs_review. The 6 true single_leaf pages (flag_fold_damage.classify_page) are not covered by any spread_split entry -- they need their own small, hand-measured bounds, not yet done. ADDENDUM 2026-09-12: the divider[4] value in every spread-format entry (plain "<season>" and "<season>:<parity>" spread_split alike) was found to be wrong -- extrapolated rather than measured when first built, and landing in blank margin past the table's own true border on every season checked. Re-measured directly against the scan on all 8 spread seasons and corrected; each entry also gained date_col_width_frac, a new field pipeline/row_detect.detect_columns() uses to bound the date-only crop at the table's border instead of the image edge (see that function's own docstring for the full mechanism). This is believed to be the primary, previously-unidentified cause of the spread format's historically poor whole-page column-wise receipts-agreement scores.
